`readmit` currently creates editable Readmission Risk Pool (RRP) projects. Each
project includes configuration, source-mapping and risk-provider scripts,
branding, and its own Shiny application. Analytical execution, state, and
products are not yet implemented.

## Create and open a project

After installing `readmit`, create a project at a new destination:

```r
readmit::rrp_project_init(
  path = "my-rrp-project",
  project_id = "my-rrp-project"
)
```

The path is relative to your current working directory unless you supply an
absolute path. Its parent directory must already exist, and the destination
must not exist, even as an empty directory. The generated files belong to you:
edit `rrp-project.dcf`, `rrp-authoring.dcf`, `_brand.yml`,
`R/produce-canonical.R`, and `R/calculate-risk.R` for your project.

The application uses `shiny`, `bslib`, and `yaml` in the environment where it
runs. Install them there, then launch the app directly from the same working
directory used in the example:

```r
install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib", "yaml"))
shiny::runApp("my-rrp-project/app")
```

The app opens with Current Risk Pool and Overview views and shows empty states
until analytical products become available in a later development stage.
